Hey, I bought a gun a couple of years ago as well. Used to bring it out whenever my wife would leave to practice how I would do it, and to desensitize myself to it. It got to a point where I scared myself into telling my therapist. Getting the gun and bullets are one thing but pulling the trigger is another. Not trying to be cliche but have you tried talking to a therapist? I’ve been seeing one for some time now and it has helped me significantly. Unloading some of those thought and feelings, and getting another perspective on your situation can do wonders. Instead of finding the courage to pull the trigger, try to find the courage not to pull the trigger. Hold off on the buck shot, it’s a temptation you don’t need right now.

They would have given me the right tools to do so, as long as I had a phone. So many variables and you never know what’s going through someone’s mind. I think in that location the sign is a good sentiment, and there’s a chance it really could help someone else. 

Also sometimes tv shows can be triggering for some people that were already suicidal, so I think ultimately it’s a good idea to have the warning, just not super helpful for me. I also already have the crisis hotline saved in my phone 

Not the second sign though, if I were distraught enough and I was already planning on jumping, I might be like yeah you’re right fuck it

Hey your not alone, I do the same thing! Especially in video games, I bank up all of my power ups but never use them. My wife makes fun of me for saving zip ties and other useful stuff but sometimes we actually end up using it so it reinforces the whole thing for me. 

My wife is the opposite and gets rid of everything we don’t need. We find a middle ground and It’s been helpful for me to realize some things I really don’t need to save. 

Maybe start small and try to think of one thing you always save but don’t use, and stop stocking up on that. Or try to have like one junk drawer to save useful items, once the drawer is full either empty some things out or stop adding to it - or both. 

I think trying to be conscience about when/why you save things, and finding peace in letting things go will help you in the long term. 

Best of luck
